description:
Casa Buonarroti in Florence combines a memorial to Michelangelo with the art and family collections assembled by his descendants. Its historic rooms reflect the ambitions of Michelangelo Buonarroti the Younger.

Early reliefs by Michelangelo sit within a broader collection of paintings, sculpture, ceramics and archaeological objects, connecting the artist’s legacy with later family patronage.

description:

description:
The Tosio Martinengo Picture Gallery occupies Palazzo Martinengo da Barco in Brescia. Its civic collection developed through private gifts and the preservation of the city’s artistic heritage.

Painting from the fifteenth to the nineteenth century gives particular prominence to the Brescian tradition, including Foppa, Savoldo, Moretto, Romanino and Ceruti.

description:
The National Archaeological Museum of Tarquinia occupies the fifteenth-century Palazzo Vitelleschi. Its formation brought together the municipal collection and the private collection of the Bruschi-Falgari family.

Finds from the ancient Etruscan city and its burial grounds place those historic collections within a broader archaeological account of Tarquinia and its territory.
